# sendgrid_domain_authentication_subuser (Resource)

Associates an authenticated domain of the parent account with a subuser, so the subuser can send from that domain without authenticating it again. Unlike `sub_user_on_behalf_of` on `sendgrid_domain_authentication`, this creates no new domain and no new DNS records. A subuser has one associated domain; the association has no update, so changing either argument replaces it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Let a subuser send from a domain the parent account has already
# authenticated. No new domain or DNS records are created.
data "sendgrid_domain_authentication" "parent" {
  domain    = "mycompany.com"
  subdomain = "em1234"
}

resource "sendgrid_subuser" "team" {
  username = "team-a"
  email    = "team-a@mycompany.com"
  password = var.subuser_password
  ips      = ["10.10.10.10"]
}

resource "sendgrid_domain_authentication_subuser" "team" {
  domain_id = data.sendgrid_domain_authentication.parent.id
  username  = sendgrid_subuser.team.username
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_id` (String) ID of the parent account's authenticated domain.
- `username` (String) Username of the subuser the domain is associated with.

### Read-Only

- `domain` (String) The associated domain.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `subdomain` (String) The subdomain of the associated domain.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
#!/bin/bash

# Import a domain association using the subuser username
terraform import sendgrid_domain_authentication_subuser.team team-a
```
